items.body:
## Summary

I'm reporting recurring reliability issues in the official Codex VS Code extension on Windows 11, using a ChatGPT Pro subscription. Codex intermittently remains at **"Thinking"** without making visible progress. On **2026-10-10 at approximately 11:27 UTC+8**, one attempt ended with an explicit stream-disconnection error.

## Exact observed error

```
stream disconnected before completion: An error occurred while processing your request. You can retry your request, or contact us through our help center at help.openai.com if the error persists. Please include the request ID 21f7c233-04a4-48a4-9a20-c0d7eaecf255 in your message.
```

**Request ID:** `21f7c233-04a4-48a4-9a20-c0d7eaecf255`

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- IDE: Visual Studio Code, official Codex extension
- Authentication/subscription: ChatGPT Pro
- Extension and VS Code versions: Not yet collected
- Model for this specific failed request: Not yet confirmed

## Observed behavior

1. The extension repeatedly gets stuck at the **Thinking** stage and sometimes never returns a usable response.
2. The user has previously observed that running Codex sessions in two VS Code windows concurrently can make this more frequent. This is a correlation, **not a confirmed trigger or root cause**.
3. On the incident above, Codex explicitly reported that its response stream disconnected before completion.
4. These issues recur and interrupt long-running research/coding workflows.

## Expected behavior

Requests should finish normally, or fail with a recoverable actionable error. If the stream is interrupted, the extension should recover/reconnect where possible without remaining indefinitely in Thinking.

## Request to maintainers

Could you inspect server/transport diagnostics for the **request ID and approximate timestamp**, and advise whether this is associated with a current backend incident or a client app-server/session-state issue? Please also advise what sanitized logs or extension diagnostics would most help reproduce/triage it.

This report does not claim a specific root cause. Additional exact version numbers and sanitized logs can be supplied if needed.

Potentially related, but not necessarily the same cause:
- #50404 (VS Code Thinking stalls / message replay)
- #41340 (stream disconnected before completion)
- #52749 (Windows repeated reconnects / stalled turns)


## Follow-up: second stream-disconnection incident (October 10, 2026)

The same user encountered a **second** failure with the same error text, under a new server Request ID. The exact time, model, extension version, and whether it affected the same thread have not yet been established.

```text
stream disconnected before completion: An error occurred while processing your request. You can retry your request, or contact us through our help center at help.openai.com if the error persists. Please include the request ID acf52ae9-fc6d-4ff2-91a4-93d00b74cb69 in your message.
```

Please correlate both request IDs: `21f7c233-04a4-48a4-9a20-c0d7eaecf255` and `acf52ae9-fc6d-4ff2-91a4-93d00b74cb69`. Similar but not confirmed to share a root cause: #52447 (503/WebSocket server-load errors), #52749 (Windows Thinking and reconnect stalls).

## Summary

`codex doctor --json` reports a `state.rollout_db_parity` warning after updating Codex CLI to `0.162.1`.

The local SQLite database integrity checks are OK, but doctor reports that the rollout file inventory and state DB thread inventory differ. The doctor output says to attach/report the issue so the samples can be inspected, but this public report is intentionally sanitized and does not include local paths or identifiers.

## Version

```text
codex-cli 0.162.1
```

The CLI was updated with:

```text
npm install -g @openai/codex
```

## Actual result

Fresh `codex doctor --json` reports overall warning status with:

```text
state.rollout_db_parity: warning
rollout files and state DB thread inventory differ
```

Aggregate details:

```text
rollout DB active files: 999
rollout DB active rows: 944
rollout DB archived files: 48
rollout DB archived rows: 48
rollout DB missing active rows: 55
rollout DB missing archived rows: 0
rollout DB duplicate rollout thread ids: 26
rollout DB duplicate DB paths: 0
rollout DB malformed file names: 0
rollout DB stale rows: 0
rollout DB scan errors: 0
rollout DB scan cap reached: false
```

Doctor issue summaries:

```text
rollout files are missing from the state DB
measured: 55 active, 0 archived
expected: every rollout file has a matching threads row

duplicate thread inventory entries found
measured: 26 duplicate rollout thread ids, 0 duplicate DB paths
expected: one rollout path and thread id per thread
```

State DB integrity was OK:

```text
state DB integrity: ok
log DB integrity: ok
goals DB integrity: ok
memories DB integrity: ok
queue DB integrity: ok
thread history DB integrity: ok
```

## Expected result

One of the following would be helpful:

- `codex doctor` provides a safe remediation command for rebuilding/reconciling thread inventory parity.
- Codex automatically reconciles/imports existing rollout files into the state DB when safe.
- If this warning can be expected after historical migrations, desktop usage, or subagent/thread-spawn workflows, doctor explains when it is safe to ignore.

## Privacy note

The full doctor report includes local paths and diagnostic identifiers, so this public issue only includes aggregate counts and high-level status.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
## Summary

In the Meetings plugin in the ChatGPT macOS app, two completed recordings of conversations with multiple people produce transcripts in which every segment is labeled `You`. The returned segment metadata contains no speaker identifiers.

Please investigate whether speaker separation is expected in the Meetings plugin, whether any settings or capture requirements apply, and whether the all-`You` result is an intended limitation or a defect.

## Observed behavior

Two anonymized recordings were checked through the connected Meetings tools after their transcripts were finalized:

- Sample A: 168 of 168 segments are labeled `You`.
- Sample B: 74 of 74 segments are labeled `You`.
- In both samples, `speaker_id`, `diarization_label`, `speaker_source`, and `speaker_email` are all `null` throughout the returned segments.
- Both transcripts have a final status.
- The display-form transcript text also labels all speech `You`.

The recordings contain conversations with multiple people according to my account of the meetings. The underlying audio has not been independently listened to or analyzed as part of this check.

The returned source metadata includes `microphone`. This alone does not establish which audio inputs were actually captured, or that only microphone audio was present.

## Environment and permissions

- Feature: Meetings plugin in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS.
- Previously recorded environment: macOS 27.0.1; ChatGPT 26.1007.21159, build 20052.
- The app and OS versions were not rechecked on the reporting date, and the exact app build used for each recording has not been established.
- A screenshot of macOS permissions checked on October 10, 2026 shows:
  - `ChatGPT` enabled in the screen and system-audio recording section.
  - `ChatGPT Meetings` and `ChatGPT` enabled in the audio-only recording section.
- The permission state at the time of the two recordings has not been verified. The current enabled permissions do not prove that system audio was captured in those recordings.

## Observed workflow

1. Record a conversation with multiple people using the Meetings plugin.
2. Finish the recording and wait for the transcript to reach its final state.
3. Inspect the transcript text and the speaker metadata returned by the Meetings tools.
4. Observe that all segments are labeled `You`, with no populated speaker identifiers.

This describes two observed samples, not a controlled reproduction with independently verified audio inputs.

## Expected behavior / clarification requested

If speaker separation is supported for this capture mode, distinguish the speakers in the transcript, using generic labels when their names are unknown. If it is not supported, please document the limitation and any relevant recording settings or audio-capture requirements.

It is currently unclear whether the issue is in speaker processing, speaker metadata returned by the connector, or the captured audio/input route. No root cause is claimed.

This report concerns the Meetings plugin. It does not establish anything about the older ChatGPT Record feature, Whisper, or the transcription API.

Only anonymized counts, field states, and environment information are included. Meeting titles, spoken content, participant information, internal identifiers, and screenshots are omitted.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.917.51856 (bundle Info.plist; build 10492; About dialog not inspected)

### What subscription do you have?

Unknown (not visible in this task)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm; macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)

### What issue are you seeing?

On 2026-10-10 in a long-running parent task, the Codex Desktop subagent/status panel displayed seven cards with the same implementation-subagent name. Six said the subagent had finished (Chinese UI: “已完成”) but each showed a different, still large “已处理 21小时…” duration; a seventh card for the same name said “正在思考” (“thinking”). This made the user think the task was stuck. At the time, the runtime agent inventory contained exactly one child with that canonical name and reported it as `interrupted`; no child was running. The parent goal had already been completed. I have not measured ongoing CPU or token use.

This is related to #38478, but the additional symptom here is several simultaneous same-name cards with different elapsed times and conflicting terminal/active text, rather than one stale row. The UI does not make clear whether it is duplicating lifecycle events or showing historical turns.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence (intermittent; not yet a deterministic reproducer):
1. In a long-running Codex Desktop task, spawn one reusable implementation subagent.
2. Send that same child two follow-up tasks, then interrupt it. The parent rollout records one spawn, two follow-up calls, and one interrupt for this child.
3. Finish the parent goal, leave/reopen the task later, and inspect the subagent/status panel.
4. Observe seven same-name entries: six “已完成” cards with different elapsed times around 21h20m–21h26m, plus one “正在思考” card.
5. Query runtime agent status: the single child is `interrupted`, with no running children.

I can provide the private thread reference and the original screenshot to maintainers through a private channel if needed.

### What is the expected behavior?

The panel should represent the child’s current execution state accurately. An interrupted child should not be shown as thinking or accumulating elapsed time. If the cards represent distinct historical turns, label them with distinct turn times/identities and freeze each completed duration; otherwise show one terminal card for the child.

### Additional information

Related reports: #38478 (completed child still shown as processing) and #40947 (stale Running subagents). I am reporting the multiple-card/conflicting-state manifestation on the newer 26.917.51856 app build. No private workspace path, thread ID, or task screenshot is included in this public issue.

items.title: [macOS desktop] Scoped permission grant still leaves credential stdin workflow blocked without an actionable approval

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Environment
- ChatGPT/Codex desktop macOS app: 26.930.61225 (CFBundleVersion 13232)
- macOS: 26.3.1 (a), build 25D771280a
- Bundled Codex CLI: 0.160.1
- Node: 24.14.0
- Projectless local chat, workspace-write sandbox, granular approval policy
- `codex login status` succeeds with `Logged in using ChatGPT`.

## Problem
A user explicitly authorized migration of their existing private Sites-backed content worker from Windows to Mac, secure local credential configuration, login-time startup, and verification using the existing ChatGPT login (no paid API keys). Migration archive integrity checks and project dependency installation succeeded, but secure credential configuration and execution remained blocked. Please investigate whether this is an approval-state propagation defect, intended policy enforcement with insufficient UX, or both.

## Observed reproduction
1. Obtain an existing private Site connection token through the authenticated Sites tool, retain it in memory, and never print it.
2. Start a workspace-local Python configuration writer in a PTY with terminal echo disabled. It waits for one JSON line and is intended to save only the connection URL/token in a workspace-local `.env.worker.json` with mode 0600.
3. Request scoped write permission for that exact config file. The permission tool returns a grant for the exact path (`scope: turn`).
4. Send the JSON through `write_stdin` to the waiting writer.
5. The tool rejects it before the writer receives the input:

```
write_stdin rejected: approval required by policy, but AskForApproval::Granular.sandbox_approval is false
```

A fresh writer process after the scoped permission grant produced the same rejection. No actionable approval prompt or explanation of the remaining requirement was supplied. Reading output from other running sessions with empty `write_stdin` worked.

## Related blockers (possibly expected sandbox limitations)
- Scoped write requests for `~/Library/LaunchAgents` and then a single prepared plist file returned no filesystem grant. A plist was prepared only in the authorized workspace; it was not installed.
- A direct minimal generation test using the existing CLI ChatGPT login failed during startup:

```
failed to run startup maintenance for logs db ... attempt to write a readonly database
Error: failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Operation not permitted (os error 1)
```

These may reflect intentional restrictions; please distinguish them from the granted workspace-file stdin failure and provide a supported least-privilege resolution.

## Expected
After granting the exact requested workspace file permission, either allow the authorized secure stdin workflow or present the precise additional approval/policy requirement and a usable way for the user to resolve it. Do not require exposing secrets in commands, chat, or logs, or enabling broad access as an undocumented workaround.

## Impact
The agent could migrate and validate the files but could not finish local worker takeover, validate heartbeat, or process existing queued work. No production drafts were overwritten, no new Site was deployed, and no paid API key was created. The user repeatedly asked the agent to act directly and then explicitly requested this report.

## Related reports
Similar rejection text appears in #51414, #51509, and #52517. This report adds the exact workspace-file scoped grant and local worker configuration case; it does not claim that the local UI had an independently verified 'On request' setting.

No credentials, private Site identifiers/URLs, migration archives, user business documents, or full session logs are included.

items.title: Classify voice session failures and record terminal outcomes
items.body:
Classify voice session failures and record terminal outcomes

## Why

Voice failure metrics lacked cause and lifecycle phase, and session durations were recorded before the final outcome was known. A failed control send could also overwrite a more specific WebRTC error.

## What changed

- Tag `codex.voice.session.failure` with bounded `cause` and `phase` values, recording at most one failure per session.
- Capture duration when stopping and emit `codex.voice.session.duration` at cleanup with a `success` or `failure` outcome.
- Carry typed WebRTC errors into the TUI, preserve existing errors when control sends fail, and avoid duplicate errors after startup failure.
- Record app-server disconnect failures for background voice sessions as well as the visible session.

## Testing

Add coverage for terminal outcome and failure metric attributes, preservation of specific startup and audio-session errors, and startup failures without duplicate control-channel errors.

items.body:
## What issue are you seeing?

GitHub connectivity failures on a dot's cloud computer prevented GitHub CLI device login and blocked the Git workflows that depended on that login. The connected GitHub integration remained separately usable.

Environment: ChatGPT dots, managed Linux cloud computer, accessed through the macOS app. GitHub CLI: `2.46.0`. Exact app and backend versions were not captured.

On October 9, 2026, around 09:56 UTC, the CLI reported:

```text
failed to authenticate via web browser: Post "https://github.com/login/device/code": dial tcp 140.82.114.4:443: connect: connection refused
```

This is an intermittent/recovery report: the latest agent-shell connectivity checks received HTTP responses, but successful CLI authentication has not been verified.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

The observed sequence was:

1. Attempt GitHub CLI browser/device login from the dot's cloud computer.
2. The request to GitHub's device-code endpoint fails with the connection-refused error above.
3. Check the three official endpoints with unauthenticated HEAD requests from the cloud shell:

```sh
for url in https://github.com https://api.github.com https://github.com/login/device/code; do
  curl -I -sS --connect-timeout 8 --max-time 12 -o /dev/null \
    -w "$url HTTP %{http_code}\n" "$url"
done
```

The HEAD requests test HTTP reachability only; they do not start or validate device authorization.

## Diagnostic timeline

All times are UTC on October 10, 2026.

- Around 01:01:59, default cloud-shell execution: all three endpoints timed out with curl exit 28 and HTTP `000`.
- Around 01:02:38, the supported elevated execution path: `api.github.com` returned HTTP 200, while `github.com` and the device-code endpoint still timed out.
- 02:53:10–02:53:21, fresh default agent-shell check: `github.com` 200, `api.github.com` 200, device-code endpoint 404; all three curl commands exited 0.
- 02:53:28–02:53:37, fresh elevated check: the same 200/200/404 results, with curl exit 0.
- A subsequent `gh auth status` still reported no logged-in GitHub hosts.

The latest checks no longer reproduce the transport failure in the agent shell. A 404 response to HEAD shows an HTTP response was received; it does not establish whether the device-flow POST or login would succeed. Login was not retried during these diagnostic checks. No network or security settings were changed.

## What is the expected behavior?

Please investigate the intermittent cloud-shell connectivity and the observed difference between execution modes. If this is an intentional network restriction, please document the supported GitHub access and recovery path and surface an actionable explanation before asking the user to complete device authorization.

## Additional information

Related observations: [#49607, section 4](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49607) and [the dots networking comment on #50986](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50986#issuecomment-6065217449). A shared root cause is unconfirmed. This standalone report is limited to cloud-computer GitHub connectivity; it does not establish a GitHub-wide outage or identify an allowlist as the cause.

items.body:
## Summary
Codex Computer Use cannot capture application windows on this Windows computer. App discovery and accessibility text extraction work, but screenshots of both Windows Notepad and Blog Studio (Electron) repeatedly time out. This prevents the requested local desktop workflow from being completed.

## Environment
- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.6466
- NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970
- NVIDIA driver 582.66 (Windows driver version 32.0.15.8266)
- Installed desktop app version reported by its built-in update check: 26.1007.21434, build 13901, production release channel; status: up_to_date
- Computer Use plugin: 26.1007.21434
- @oai/sky: 0.7.6
- Affected apps: Windows Notepad and Blog Studio 0.3.53 (Electron)

## Steps to reproduce
1. On an unlocked local Windows desktop, open Notepad and bring its window to the foreground.
2. Initialize the bundled @oai/sky client in node_repl.
3. Obtain the actual Notepad Window from sky.list_windows(), then sky.get_window().
4. Call sky.get_window_state({window, include_screenshot:true, include_text:true}).
5. Refresh window selection, activate the window, and retry: capture fails again.
6. Repeat for the Electron app: the same failure occurs.

## Expected behavior
A screenshot of the selected window is returned, with usable geometry for UI interaction.

## Actual behavior
Captures fail with:
- FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel
- window capture timed out: timed out waiting on channel

items.title: [macOS][Computer History] IntelliJ workflow triggers 600–700% recorder CPU and AX error flood; persists after pause

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### App and environment

- ChatGPT/Codex Desktop: **26.1007.21159 (build 20052)**, read from the installed app plist.
- Computer Use helper: **26.1005.1001425 (build 1001425)**, bundle identifier `com.openai.sky.CUAService`.
- macOS: **27.0.1 (26A434)**, ARM64; 18 logical CPUs.
- IntelliJ IDEA: **2026.1.2**, bundle identifier `com.jetbrains.intellij`.
- Subscription: not included.
- Observed on **2026-10-10**, timestamps below in **UTC+08:00**.

### Problem

With **Computer History running**, `SkyComputerUseService` consumed sustained multi-core CPU while emitting a flood of `AccessibilitySupport.UIElementError` errors. IntelliJ IDEA was actively used during the initial incident. After restarting the helper and re-enabling history, the accessibility-error flood and high CPU recurred around manual IDEA interactions.

Original spot CPU readings included **567.6%** (Activity Monitor) and **593.9%** (`ps`). In the new recorder process after the restart, readings reached **286.1%, 722.6%, and 630.7%**. Percentages use the macOS per-core convention.

The samples repeatedly show background threads traversing the same recursive helper code around `Sequence.compactMap`, with AX attribute reads and Swift object-management/copying work. The binary is not fully symbolicated, so this report does **not** establish a source-level infinite loop or the exact offending UI element.

### Observed workflow / reproduction

This is an observed reproduction, not yet a minimal deterministic reproducer:

1. Enable Computer History with applications and websites observed by default, and no allowlist/blocklist entries.
2. Use IntelliJ IDEA, including editor, Commit/diff, and Git Log interfaces.
3. Observe sustained high CPU from the recorder and repeated accessibility errors.
4. Pause Computer History without terminating the helper: the ongoing high CPU and error flood persist.
5. Temporarily exclude `com.jetbrains.intellij` without restarting the already-unhealthy process: the high CPU persists.
6. Terminate the unhealthy helper, restart it, and re-enable Computer History through Settings.
7. Initially exclude IDEA, then restore allowing IDEA.
8. Manually use IDEA in the foreground, switching/scrolling editor or Git-related interfaces.
9. Observe the error flood and high CPU recur in the **new recorder PID**. Its native samples show the same recursive code offsets and AX-reading work.

The original high CPU predates diagnostic UI automation. The restart-phase reproduction also included some read-only Computer Use AX inspections/attempted window operations before the user manually interacted with IDEA. Therefore the second phase is not a pure background-only reproduction.

### Measurements

| Window / experiment | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Original process, 10:27:32.570–10:30:32.556 | **183,801** UIElementError entries in approximately 180 seconds, about **1,021/sec** |
| Earlier complete minute, 10:24 | **100,401** UIElementError entries |
| Earlier complete minute, 10:25 | **147,066** UIElementError entries |
| Pause test, 10:30:52–10:31:12 | CPU remained approximately **517–540%**; cumulative CPU time increased by about **104.6 seconds** over 20 seconds |
| Error window during pause, 10:31:01–10:31:26 | **19,006** UIElementError entries in 25 seconds |
| Temporary IDEA exclusion on unhealthy original process, 10:31:35–10:31:55 | CPU approximately **450–502%**; cumulative CPU time increased by about **93.2 seconds** over 20 seconds |
| New actual recorder, 10:33:31–10:35:00 | **104** UIElementError entries, far below the later flood |
| New actual recorder, 10:35:51.127–10:36:36.121 | **88,692** UIElementError entries in approximately 45 seconds, about **1,971/sec** |
| Later spot readings of new actual recorder | **286.1%, 722.6%, 630.7% CPU** |

Computer History persisted IDEA selection/window events starting at **10:36:00** in this phase. The error window starts before the first persisted IDEA event; this does not prove the exact triggering instant.

Previously recorded IDEA full-tree text reached **76,794 characters / 2,991 lines**. Those are text-line counts, **not** a count of UI controls.

### Native sampling and representative log evidence

The original service and its parent relationship were confirmed with `ps`. IDEA remained running throughout the investigation. A native sample of IDEA also showed it receiving macOS accessibility attribute queries, including `_AXXMIGCopyAttributeValue` and `_AXXMIGGetAttributeValueCount`.

Representative sanitized recorder errors:

```text
2026-10-10 10:27:32.570 E SkyComputerUseService[<original-recorder>:<thread>]
[inc.software.app:UIElement]
Error Domain=AccessibilitySupport.UIElementError Code=0

2026-10-10 10:35:51.127 E SkyComputerUseService[<new-recorder>:<thread>]
[inc.software.app:UIElement]
Error Domain=AccessibilitySupport.UIElementError Code=0
```

Both `UIElement` and `TransformedUIElement` categories emit these errors. The custom error-domain code is not interpreted as a permission failure or a successful operation.

Repeated ancestor/descendant structure in multiple original-process samples, including a sample while history was paused:

```text
SkyComputerUseService + 0x64f474
  Sequence.compactMap<A>(_:)
    Sequence._compactMap<A>(_:)
      SkyComputerUseService + 0x6506fc
        SkyComputerUseService + 0x64f68c
          SkyComputerUseService + 0x64f474
            Sequence.compactMap<A>(_:)
              Sequence._compactMap<A>(_:)
                SkyComputerUseService + 0x6506fc
                  SkyComputerUseService + 0x64f68c
                    SkyComputerUseService + 0x64f474
                      ... repeated descendants ...
```

Original/paused samples contained this recursive code in **11–13 thread sections**. This is an observation of multiple sampled threads, not proof that all of them were simultaneously executing on-CPU.

Other captured frames included:

```text
AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue
_AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue
AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues
AXUIElementCopyAttributeNames
_AXMIGGetAttributeValueCount
swift_retain / swift_release
swift_bridgeObjectRetain / swift_bridgeObjectRelease
_platform_memmove
Collection.firstIndex(where:)
Array.subscript.read
```

The new-recorder sample again included the same `+0x64f474` recursive code and AX calls. Pausing did not remove this signature from the original process.

### Important diagnostic limitation: two helper instances during restart

During diagnosis, a helper was manually launched after terminating the original. When history was subsequently enabled in Settings, the desktop app started a **separate actual recorder**, parented to ChatGPT.

An early reported 5–6% CPU baseline was measured against the manually launched auxiliary instance and is **not a valid CPU baseline for the actual recorder**. That number is deliberately excluded from the measurement table. The error counts above were grouped by PID; the post-restart high-CPU readings and samples were taken from the actual recorder. The manually launched extra helper was then terminated.

This limits any claim of a perfectly controlled exclusion/allowance CPU A/B test. Nonetheless, the actual new recorder showed the same high-CPU/error signature after the observed IDEA workflow.

### Expected behavior

- Background accessibility collection should have bounded CPU and traversal work.
- Stale/inaccessible UI elements should not cause thousands of repeated errors per second.
- Pausing history or excluding an application should promptly cancel outstanding collection work for that scope.
- Restarting and resuming should not quickly recreate runaway work during ordinary IDE interaction.

### Requested investigation

Please investigate cancellation of in-flight AX traversal/conversion tasks, traversal bounds, invalid-element handling, and concurrent work accumulation. Please advise which additional targeted diagnostic would best identify the exact IDEA control or helper code path.

IDEA is a strong suspected trigger, but the exact control, deterministic trigger, and responsibility between helper/IDE/macOS are unresolved. We have not verified that excluding IDEA **followed by a fresh recorder restart** permanently prevents recurrence.

Potentially related: **#38873** (Computer History traversal freezes IntelliJ Git Log). This report adds multi-core recorder CPU, very high AX-error volume, persistence after pause/exclusion, and recurrence in a new recorder process. It does not include the exact IDEA EDT Git-graph stack documented in #38873, so equivalence is not assumed.

The user authorized submitting this report. The report was prepared with agent assistance from local process snapshots, native samples, unified logs, and Computer History metadata. Technical excerpts are included inline; raw session/event-stream content, project source, account identifiers, and personal workspace paths are omitted. Full raw local diagnostic files have not been uploaded.

items.title: Make code-mode `exit()` stop the entire cell
items.body:
Make code-mode `exit()` stop the entire cell

## Why

A catchable exception lets JavaScript continue after `exit()`, including in `catch`, `finally`, and queued promise callbacks. Exiting should finish the cell successfully without further output or state changes.

## What changed

- Terminate V8 execution when `exit()` is called and complete the cell even if its module promise remains pending.
- Guard host callbacks against effects after exit, including when getters or value conversion request exit.
- Preserve stored writes made before exit and suppress errors when exit occurs during exception formatting.

## Testing

Add regression tests for synchronous and asynchronous exit, timers, parallel promises, value conversion, exception getters, and resuming after a yield and tool response. Verify that only prior output and stored writes survive, and separately exercise host guards while JavaScript continues running.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0`, verified with `Get-AppxPackage`.
Desktop product version recorded by the app's update check during the earlier investigation: `26.1007.21434`, build `13901`, production channel.
Actual desktop backend: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`, independently verified again on October 10, 2026.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64, OS version `10.0.26300.0`, PowerShell `7.6.3`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The Settings > Configuration page displays an unknown session feature:

```text
Codex is ignoring 1 unrecognized configuration setting. Check for typos or deprecated settings.
session-flags: features.code_mode_tool_description_first is ignored.
```

The same page also displays:

```text
[features.guardianv2].thread_context is deprecated and ignored.
Thread-owned Guardian context is always enabled. Remove thread_context from [features.guardianv2] in config.toml, including profile overrides.
```

Neither feature occurs in the current user `config.toml`. Earlier read-only inspection of the installed desktop bundle found a dynamic session-feature injection path for `code_mode_tool_description_first`. A newly started instance of the same backend successfully read the user configuration without reproducing these two desktop-session warnings. The live outgoing desktop request was not captured, so the complete override provenance remains unconfirmed.

The user also encounters a separate, opaque command rejection under Full access. The original session transcript confirms that deletion of one agent-created, ordinary **53-byte test file** used this command shape:

```powershell
Remove-Item -LiteralPath 'C:\example-workspace\.runtime\.cache\policy-probe-disposable.txt' -Force
```

The displayed path is anonymized. It is not a user-data target. The command was rejected before process creation:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(... rejected: blocked by policy)" }
```

The original same-command retry remained rejected. The file is still present. No matching safety condition, rule identifier, or approval action appeared in the error.

**These are separate observations. No evidence establishes that the ignored/deprecated feature warnings cause the command rejection.**

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed in the affected desktop session:

1. Open Settings > Configuration after working in an existing local chat.
2. Observe the unknown `session-flags` warning and Guardian deprecation notice despite the absence of those keys from the user configuration.
3. With effective `approval_policy = "never"` and `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, ask the agent to remove a disposable file it created in the workspace cache.
4. The `Remove-Item ... -Force` call returns the generic policy rejection above.

The single-file deletion was actually attempted and rejected on this installation. This is not a claimed clean-install or universally reproducible desktop example. Restarting/reinstalling has not been verified as a repair here. This reporting task did not retry deletion or change approval settings.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Desktop-generated feature overrides should match the bundled backend's supported schema.
- Configuration warnings should identify app/session overrides and offer an actionable remedy, rather than directing users to edit a file that lacks the setting.
- When a command safety check rejects forced deletion, the error should identify that condition and explain the supported approval route.
- Full access wording should make the interaction with approval policy clear.

### Additional information

Earlier local diagnostics verified a valid OpenAI backend signature and matching package block-map hashes for the desktop executable, frontend archive, and backend. No installation corruption was identified. A separate fresh backend returned `requirements: null` from `configRequirements/read`; this does not establish all effective policy layers of the live desktop process.

A prior unsupported `computer_use.windows.always_allowed_app_ids` configuration was backed up and removed. Independent configuration checks confirmed that its warning disappeared and the effective configuration was unchanged. The original deletion retry still failed afterward.

The matching public backend tag supplies a plausible explanation for the forced-delete rejection:

- [Forced-delete classifier](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/shell-command/src/command_safety/windows_dangerous_commands.rs#L223): delete cmdlet plus `-Force`.
- [Windows dangerous-command mapping](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/shell-command/src/command_safety/is_dangerous_command.rs#L74): maps the result to `Other`.
- [Approval decision](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs#L794): `Never` returns `Forbidden`; `OnRequest` returns `Prompt`.
- [Rejection text](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs#L1110): `Other` becomes only `blocked by policy`.

This source match is not a captured runtime decision trace. Please clarify the supported desktop approval setting for this case, without a broad allow rule or a bypass.

Related reports: #50526 covers the Guardian warning; #45403 covers Windows forced cleanup and opaque denial; #47043 covers another unknown desktop session feature. A search did not find a report for the exact `code_mode_tool_description_first` key. The new compatibility warning is the primary addition in this report; the related observations are included to avoid incorrectly attributing the rejection to the warnings.

Prepared by a Codex assistant at the affected user's explicit request. No credentials, account identifiers, actual local paths, project names, raw configuration, logs, or chat history are attached.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI and desktop, specifically remote Streamable HTTP MCP servers.

### What feature would you like to see?

Add a per-server HTTP/3 policy for Streamable HTTP MCP connections:

```toml
[mcp_servers.example]
url = "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
http3 = "prefer" # auto | prefer | require
```

Proposed semantics:

- `auto` (and omission): preserve today's HTTP/1.1-or-HTTP/2 behavior exactly.
- `prefer`: use HTTP/3 when the resolved outbound route and executor support it; otherwise use today's transport. A fallback must occur before request dispatch, not by replaying an ambiguous MCP or OAuth POST.
- `require`: use HTTP/3 for the MCP connection and its OAuth/discovery traffic, or fail closed with a diagnostic. Never bypass a configured proxy to satisfy this mode.

This would be useful for MCP servers behind HTTP/3-capable edges, especially on lossy or changing networks where QUIC can avoid some TCP head-of-line and reconnection costs. The explicit modes let operators retain current behavior, opt into opportunistic use, or verify that an HTTP/3 path is actually in use.

### Additional information

I traced the current implementation on `main` at `5ef96ab2785f3ecddf279639eff7b1b42c906fa4`. The smallest coherent Rust design appears to be:

1. Add a typed `auto | prefer | require` field to the Streamable HTTP branch of `RawMcpServerConfig` / `McpServerTransportConfig` in `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs`. Reject it for stdio. Omission remains `auto`, and the default is omitted from serialization.
2. Bind the server policy once around the existing `Arc<dyn codex_exec_server::HttpClient>` selected by `McpRuntimeContext`. This keeps rmcp constructors unchanged and applies the same rule to MCP POST/SSE/DELETE and OAuth discovery, registration, token exchange, refresh, and login.
3. Carry a transport-neutral HTTP-version policy in `HttpRequestParams` (`codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs`) so remote executors enforce it on the machine that owns the route. `auto` stays wire-compatible. `require` must reject an executor that does not advertise support; `prefer` must either reject or explicitly diagnose a downgrade rather than silently claiming HTTP/3.
4. Enforce the policy only after the existing route-aware client resolves direct/proxy/managed routing. Pool/cache identity must include effective transport policy. Redirects must be route-resolved again. Existing proxy authentication, custom CA, TLS backend, timeout, cancellation, SSE, and credential-stripping rules remain authoritative.

The important replay invariant is:

```text
HTTP/3 setup fails and the backend proves no request was dispatched
  -> prefer may use the existing transport

request bytes may have been sent, dispatch is unknown, or a response stream fails
  -> return the transport error; never replay merely because no response headers arrived
```

A buffered body is physically replayable but not necessarily semantically safe. MCP tool calls, OAuth registration, and token requests may mutate state.

Relevant current boundaries:

- Streamable HTTP startup chooses the injected client in `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/rmcp_client.rs`.
- Local/remote client selection lives in `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/runtime.rs`.
- Local route-aware execution and pooling live in `codex-rs/exec-server/src/client/route_aware_http_client.rs` and `codex-rs/http-client/src/route_aware_client_pool.rs`.
- The generic executor HTTP envelope currently has no HTTP-version field.
- CLI `codex mcp login` constructs its own route-aware client, so an implementation confined to MCP startup would miss part of OAuth.

Current backend constraint: the workspace pins reqwest 0.12.28. Its `http3` feature and `ClientBuilder::http3_prior_knowledge()` are experimental and require `--cfg reqwest_unstable`; the latter is HTTP/3-only rather than a complete `prefer` policy. `codex-tcp-tunnel` already uses h3/quinn for MASQUE CONNECT, but it does not implement the general request, redirect, OAuth, proxy, custom-CA, SSE, cancellation, or pooling contracts needed here. Reusing it directly would create a second incomplete HTTP stack.

Suggested acceptance tests:

- Config/schema/default/stdio validation and old fixture compatibility.
- Local and remote-executor capability matrices, including old executors.
- Recording-client coverage for buffered and streamed MCP plus OAuth/login requests.
- Route tests for direct, proxy, managed route, plaintext, redirects, custom CA, proxy auth, and TLS backend selection.
- A transport-state regression test proving no fallback after request bytes may have been dispatched.
- Real HTTP/3 negotiation, connection reuse, incremental SSE, and `require` failure tests once a supported backend is selected.

I did not open a code PR because `docs/contributing.md` asks external contributors to provide detailed analysis/design through issues and states that external PRs are not accepted.

items.body:
## Summary

Ordinary sandboxed PowerShell commands in the Windows desktop app fail before the command starts with:

```
helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```

Sandbox setup refresh reports Windows sharing violation (os error 32) when validating read/execute access on loaded runtime files. Related reports: #52172 and #52033. This report adds a controlled feature-isolation result: disabling browser/computer-use did not resolve ordinary execution, and the next failure moved to node.exe used by the application's tools MCP server.

## Environment

- Windows 11, OS 10.0.26200, build 26200.
- Installed Store package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0 (package version, not About-dialog version).
- Bundled CLI previously verified: 0.162.0-alpha.2.
- CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex: Running, automatic startup.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

1. Open the installed desktop application and a local Windows project.
2. Request a harmless ordinary sandboxed command such as `Write-Output 'ORDINARY_EXEC_RETEST'`.
3. Observe initialization failure before PowerShell runs.
4. Inspect the sandbox log for runtime read/execute validation and error 32.

Expected: ordinary approved-scope commands execute under the intended sandbox with application features restored. An offline setup pass is not sufficient.

## Diagnostic evidence (paths redacted)

The log reports:

```
runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on <runtime-file>:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

Affected runtime files observed across tests:
- `runtimes/cua_node/<runtime-id>/bin/node_repl.exe`
- `runtimes/cua_node/<runtime-id>/bin/node_modules/@oai/sky/bin/windows/swift/x64/VCRUNTIME140_1.dll`
- `runtimes/cua_node/<runtime-id>/bin/node.exe`

The node.exe processes were traced via process-parent inspection to:
```
cmd.exe /d /s /c call ./scripts/launch_codex_app_tools_mcp.cmd ./server.mjs
node.exe ./server.mjs
```

This means not all loaded runtime holders belong to browser/computer-use features.

## Controlled tests and rollback

- Earlier offline repair passed while the app was closed, but the failure returned after app reopening.
- Temporarily used official requirements to set browser_use, browser_use_external, browser_use_full_cdp_access, in_app_browser and computer_use to false. CLI effective feature output confirmed all five false.
- First isolation still failed on the Swift DLL; the independently running Swift helper had not been included in shutdown.
- Repeated once after explicitly stopping the verified app and exact node_repl/Swift helper paths. At probe start, exact node_repl and Swift helper counts were zero. Sandbox failed on node.exe at 2026-10-10 09:19:41 Asia/Shanghai.
- A Swift helper was again present by the end of that test; therefore the feature policy did not guarantee the absence of every native helper.
- Removed only the temporary requirements file created by the test, restored its original absence, and verified app reopening. Worker terminated at 09:20:08.
- Ordinary execution retest after restoration failed again at approximately 09:20:34.
- Approved out-of-sandbox diagnostic commands can execute; that is not a workaround claimed as a sandbox fix.

No permanent sandbox/security weakening, app-data reset, runtime binary patch or sandbox-secret deletion was performed in this isolation test.

## Assessment and request

The observations establish a loaded-runtime sharing violation during setup refresh, but do not prove the precise internal defect or that a specific newer version fixes it.

Please investigate runtime ACL-refresh/lifecycle ordering while desktop helpers hold those files. Please provide a supported recovery path preserving sandbox boundaries and local project/history. Success should be verified with ordinary execution after app reopening with original features restored.

This report is intentionally sanitized: no usernames, absolute personal paths, account information, project content, authentication data or full conversation transcript are attached.

items.title: ChatGPT GitHub connector cannot read ~60 MB PDF from private repo (binary-safe document handoff)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

items.body:
## Summary

In ChatGPT web with the GitHub connector installed and authorized for a **private repository**, repository browsing and file metadata work, but ChatGPT cannot retrieve a large PDF's content for document Q&A. A `fetch_file` request with `encoding: "base64"` returns a valid blob SHA and encoding but an **empty content string**; the generic GitHub fetch endpoint does not support returning large non-UTF-8/binary responses.

This blocks a natural workflow: "Read section 3.7 of the PDF in my private GitHub repository and teach/explain it," despite the assistant locating the precise file and having access to its metadata.

## Reproduction (anonymized)

1. Connect GitHub to ChatGPT and grant access to a private repository containing a PDF approximately **60,438,325 bytes (~60 MB)**.
2. Ask ChatGPT to read a specific chapter/section of that PDF, referring to its path within the repository.
3. List the repository's directories and the file with GitHub `fetch`/Contents API: **success**; name, size, blob SHA and contents metadata are visible.
4. Call `fetch_file` with the repository path and `encoding: "base64"`: tool output contains a blob SHA and `encoding: "base64"`, but `content.length === 0` (including with and without line-range parameters).
5. Attempt the generic `fetch` route for raw PDF content: binary/non-UTF-8 responses are unsupported.
6. ChatGPT can only teach the topic from outside information; it cannot validate against the actual PDF text, formulas, diagrams, and page numbering.

**No private repository URL, name, filename, or document content is included here.** The exact failure stage/root cause has not been confirmed.

## Expected behavior

- The GitHub connector should support authenticated, **binary-safe file retrieval** from private repositories for ordinary PDFs, ideally returning a downloadable file reference/stream instead of attempting to place binary/base64 content in the LLM text-response budget.
- Allow a direct handoff to ChatGPT's PDF document-reading/conversion tools (e.g. PDF-to-Markdown/page rendering), supporting retrieval of selected pages/chapters without re-uploading the file manually.
- If retrieval fails due to file size, MIME type, or quota, give a clear explicit diagnostic instead of an empty content body.

## Why this matters

A common educational/research workflow is to keep source textbooks, lecture slides, and technical documents in a connected private GitHub repository and ask for chapter-specific explanations. Requiring a manual browser download and re-upload on every new chat substantially reduces connector usefulness.

GitHub itself supports raw download of files in this size range; this looks like a ChatGPT connector / file-handoff limitation rather than a repository permission issue.

Related (but not identical) reports: #43923 (private binary attachment access), #38099 (connector response-size/truncation issues), #45448 (binary file handoff in the opposite direction).

## Environment

- Client: ChatGPT web
- Integration: GitHub connector; private repository already authorized
- File type: PDF (binary)
- File size: ~60 MB
- Observed: October 2026

Please consider this a feature request/bug report for authenticated binary file download and downstream document-parser handoff from GitHub.

items.title: [Windows][Computer Use] Native APIs disabled / node_repl timeout after update - workaround by rollback + runtime rebuild

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Affected installed package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0. Working after rollback: 26.930.7945.0. These are package versions documented in the diagnostic report; the About dialog was not separately recorded.

### What subscription do you have?

Not specified in the diagnostic report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, build 10.0.26300.9550; final agent environment: Windows native.

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

On Windows 11, native Computer Use stopped working after a ChatGPT/Codex desktop app update. Browser automation through the Chrome/Edge extension still worked, but native Windows automation reported:

```text
Native computer APIs are disabled.
```

The managed `node_repl` also failed on minimal JavaScript with:

```text
js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request
```

This interrupted my work for approximately a day and a half. I am sharing the diagnosis and recovery so other affected users and maintainers can compare their results.

A recovery on this machine was achieved by rolling back the desktop app, rebuilding generated Computer Use plugins/runtime, and initializing the native `@oai/sky` backend in a fresh session. **This is a user-verified workaround on one machine, not an official fix or a universal recovery procedure.** The exact internal root cause remains unproven.

## Environment and versions

| Component | Observed version or state |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300.9550 |
| Affected installed package | OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0 |
| Version also present in historical logs/sessions | 26.1002.52244; distinct from the installed package version |
| Working rollback | OpenAI.Codex 26.930.7945.0 |
| computer-use | 26.930.61225 |
| unified-computer-use | 26.930.61225 |
| Regenerated cua_node runtime | 71e3f41277f96d73 |
| Bundled Node | v24.21.0 |
| @oai/sky | 0.7.5 |
| Final agent environment | Windows native |
| WSL diagnostic comparison | WSL 3.0.1.0, Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, WSL2, bwrap available |

These versions describe the affected and recovered setup; they are not a claim about the latest available release.

## Positive control and diagnostic evidence

Using the same bundled `node.exe` outside the managed `node_repl`, importing `@oai/sky` succeeded:

```text
SKY_IMPORT_OK
EXIT_CODE: 0
```

This argues against a simple missing/broken `@oai/sky` package or straightforward missing-DLL explanation, but does not prove every dependency is healthy.

Earlier logs contained `runtime read/execute validation failed`, `os error 32` while updating ACLs for `node_repl.exe` and `VCRUNTIME140_1.dll`, and `setup refresh had errors`. The evidence does not establish these as the cause of the managed-REPL timeout.

The `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` service was Running, with StartMode Auto and ExitCode 0. That rules out a simply stopped service, but does not by itself establish that Computer Use works.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. After the desktop update, request native Windows Computer Use in a local Windows session.
2. Observe `Native computer APIs are disabled.`, while browser-extension automation remains functional.
3. Try a minimal JavaScript call in the managed `node_repl`; it times out and resets the kernel.
4. Try the installed Computer Use skill's native initialization:

```js
if (!globalThis.sky) {
  const { sky } = await import("@oai/sky");
  globalThis.sky = sky;
}
```

The import inside the managed REPL could not be confirmed because the call timed out and reset the kernel. These steps describe one affected setup, not a clean-install reproduction established on multiple machines.

### What is the expected behavior?

Native Windows Computer Use should remain available after a desktop app update. The managed node_repl should execute minimal JavaScript and initialize @oai/sky without timing out, then enumerate and interact with normal, non-elevated Windows applications when the native backend is enabled.

### Additional information

## Recovery that worked on this machine

1. Roll back the desktop app to `26.930.7945.0`.
2. Fully close ChatGPT/Codex and its helper processes.
3. Move aside as backups, rather than delete, these generated directories:
   - `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\plugins\cache\openai-bundled`
   - `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.tmp\bundled-marketplaces\openai-bundled`
   - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node`
4. Restart the app and allow it to regenerate the components.
5. Verify plugin versions `26.930.61225` and a new `cua_node` runtime containing `node.exe`, `node_repl.exe`, and `@oai/sky`.
6. During regeneration, logs briefly showed `os error 3` (path not found) for tool discovery, then repaired/reinstalled state and:

```text
server=node_repl status=ready
server=cua_repl status=ready
computer-use native pipe startup ready
```

7. Start a fresh Computer Use session. GPT-6 Astra was used for the successful test; this does not establish a model-specific cause or fix.
8. Initialize `@oai/sky` explicitly and run `await sky.list_apps();`.
9. Verify harmless native interaction in a non-elevated application such as Notepad.

The rollback and regeneration were performed together, so their individual contributions to recovery were not isolated.

## Final verification

- `sky.list_apps()` enumerated real Windows applications.
- Native Computer Use activated Notepad and typed exactly `PRUEBA COMPUTER USE OK` in a new tab, leaving it unsaved.
- Native window screenshots worked.
- Chrome/Edge browser automation continued to work.

## Separate limitation: elevated applications

SAP Business One runs as Administrator in this environment. It could be detected, activated, and captured, but clicks did not produce visible changes. Input from a lower-integrity automation process may be blocked by Windows integrity/UIPI. This is recorded separately from the successful recovery in normal Windows applications; the precise input-blocking mechanism was not independently traced.

## Diagnosis and requested investigation

The evidence is consistent with a regression or state-consistency problem in the managed `node_repl` / sandbox / Computer Use plugin integration, possibly involving stale or mixed generated state after an update. The internal root cause is not proven.

Please investigate:

1. Managed `node_repl` timeouts while the same bundled Node imports `@oai/sky` successfully outside the managed REPL.
2. Plugin/runtime consistency after desktop upgrades and downgrades.
3. Why `node_repl` / `cua_repl` can report ready while a session receives `Native computer APIs are disabled.`.
4. Automatic invalidation or regeneration of incompatible generated artifacts after version changes.
5. Robust retry after transient `os error 3` during reconstruction.
6. Diagnostics that distinguish browser availability, native API availability, and session or integrity-level restrictions.

No DCOM changes, UAC disabling, DLL replacement, manual ACL editing, or deletion of authentication/session data was needed for this recovery.

## Related reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51719 - Native Computer Use / Node REPL fails during sandbox setup with os error 32; overlaps with the historical log evidence here.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50876 - Computer Use failures across a desktop update.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49742 - Browser-only Computer Use surface despite an enabled native backend.

These reports have overlapping symptoms; a shared root cause has not been established. This report adds the managed-REPL versus bundled-Node control test and the rollback/regeneration outcome on the affected machine.

items.title: Allow model catalogs to override incremental tool notices
items.body:
Allow model catalogs to override incremental tool notices

## What changed

Add `model_messages.tools.incremental_tools` overrides for the update hint, tool and namespace removal headers, and namespace instruction update and clearing messages. Missing, null, or over-512-byte values fall back to bundled wording; empty strings omit static text while retaining runtime names and instructions.

items.body:
Bug report: Windows sandbox setup fails because Codex's own helpers occupy the runtime binaries it tries to ACL

**Suggested title:** `Windows sandbox provisioning always fails: setup tries to update ACLs on runtime binaries that Codex itself is executing (os error 32)`

## Summary

On Windows, the sandboxed (default / "ask for approval") execution mode is unusable: every command fails with

```
Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```

The sandbox provisioning step (`codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe`) aborts because it cannot open runtime
executables for an ACL update while those same executables are running:

```
runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\<hash>\bin\node.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update: 另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。 (os error 32)
```

Windows does not allow modifying the security descriptor of a file that is currently mapped as an image
(a running executable). Because Codex itself launches several helper processes out of that same runtime
directory, this is a permanent conflict, not a transient race.

## Environment

- App: display name **ChatGPT**, package identity **OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0** (x64, Microsoft Store build)
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), display language zh-CN
- Config: `~/.codex/config.toml` → `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`; default permission profile (workspace-write)
- Not reproducible in Full access mode (that path does not perform sandbox provisioning)
- No third-party endpoint protection installed (`codex doctor` reports `no supported endpoint protection detected`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the app from the Microsoft Store and leave the execution mode at its default (sandboxed / ask-for-approval).
2. Open any chat and ask the agent to run a trivial command, e.g. `echo hi`.
3. The command fails immediately with `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`.

Reproduced consistently across app restarts, and also on a fresh install.

## Evidence

`~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.<date>.log` — the provisioning run aborts on the runtime validation:

```
[2026-10-09 19:19:41.575 codex.exe] setup refresh: spawning ...\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe (cwd=..., payload_len=3196)
[2026-10-09T11:19:41.642+00:00] failed to grant non-inheriting read-attributes ACE on user profile C:\Users\<user>:
    open ACL target for root-only update: 另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。 (os error 32); continuing setup
[2026-10-09T11:19:41.676+00:00] runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on
    ...\runtimes\cua_node\<hash>\bin\node_repl.exe: open ACL target ...
[2026-10-09T11:19:41.680+00:00] setup refresh completed with errors: [...]
[2026-10-09T11:19:41.680+00:00] setup error: setup refresh had errors
[2026-10-09 19:19:41.680 codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe] setup error: setup refresh had errors
[2026-10-09 19:19:41.688 codex.exe] setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
```

Processes running out of the same runtime directory at that moment (all launched by the app itself):

```
node_repl.exe                                             × 5
node.exe  ...\@oai\cua-repl\bin\cua-repl.mjs              × 2
codex-computer-use-swift.exe  ...\@oai\sky\bin\...        × 1
```

The failure target moves between files as different helpers start and stop — we first observed it on
`bin\node.exe`, later on `bin\node_repl.exe` — which confirms the mechanism: **whichever runtime binary
Codex is currently executing cannot also be ACL-updated by the setup step.**

The ACL itself is already correct on these files (`BUILTIN\Users`/`CodexSandboxUsers` already have inherited
read+execute), so the update is not needed for correctness — but the code path still treats the failed open
as fatal.

## Root cause

`codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` performs a fatal "runtime read/execute validation" that opens each runtime
binary with a root-only ACL update (`WRITE_DAC`). For a running image that open fails with
`ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION (32)`. Since the app always keeps helper processes alive from the `cua_node` runtime
(the app-tools MCP server, the node REPL server, the cua-repl server, computer-use helper), the provisioning
step has no reliable window in which it can succeed.

## Suggested fix

1. Treat `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` during the runtime ACL validation as **non-fatal**
   when the effective ACL already grants the required read/execute access (i.e., verify access instead of
   unconditionally re-applying it).
2. Avoid running helper processes from a directory whose executables the sandbox setup needs to modify —
   e.g. run the MCP servers/helpers from the primary runtime bundle (`~/.cache/codex-runtimes/...`), or
   copy the sandbox runtime binaries to a per-provisioning location.
3. Alternatively, validate ACLs by reading the DACL rather than opening the file for update.

## Workaround (user side)

- No configuration change fixes it. Once the mode is set to **Full access** (no sandbox), commands work
  normally — that path does not perform provisioning.
- Killing the helper processes unlocks the files, but the app restarts them, so the sandbox breaks again
  within minutes. Not a stable workaround.

## Notes

- Related: the store package's `AppxManifest.xml` declares only `<Resource Language="en-US" />`, while the
  package ships `locales/zh-CN.pak` and `native-menu-locales/zh-CN.json`; the UI therefore stays English on a
  Chinese system even with `[desktop] localeOverride = "zh-CN"` set. (Separate issue, may be worth a look.)
- `codex doctor` on this machine reports: `✗ sandbox  elevated Windows sandbox provisioning recorded a structured failure`.

items.body:
## Environment

- Windows 10
- Codex Desktop: 26.1007.21434
- CLI version observed during troubleshooting: 0.162.1
- Task created by dot using a saved cloud coding environment

## Observed behavior

An existing cloud task was inconsistently discoverable in the Recents sidebar. The task had also been successfully renamed to a title containing an emoji.

Corrected sequence from the affected session:

1. Immediately after creation, the task was absent from the sidebar.
2. Many hours later, after returning to the app, I saw it in the sidebar. The exact time it first appeared is unknown.
3. After restarting the desktop app, it was missing again.
4. Direct backend reads of the same persisted task still succeeded. Its latest recorded turn was completed, so the missing sidebar entry did not mean the task had been deleted.
5. Dot surfaced the same existing task again in our chat. I could open it there while it was initially still absent from the sidebar.
6. After opening it directly from the chat, I saw it in Recents again. Its reappearance was visually confirmed in the current session.

## Expected behavior

A successfully created cloud task should be discoverable promptly, and existing accessible tasks should remain discoverable after restarting the app.

## Observed workaround

Opening the existing task directly from the dot chat was followed by its reappearance in Recents. I have not established whether that visibility survives another restart.

## Scope

This is one observed sequence on an existing installation, not a deterministic minimal reproduction. The root cause is unknown. The title's emoji is included only as context; no causal connection has been established.

## Related reports

- #51675: macOS cloud tasks missing after restart, with individual entries returning after direct reads.
- #51740: Windows cloud tasks disappearing again after restart, with additional coordination errors.
- #49964: dot-created cloud tasks missing from web Recents.

This report adds the Windows 10 / 26.1007.21434 observation, including initial absence, appearance noticed hours later, disappearance after restart, and reappearance after opening the task from chat. A shared cause has not been established; please consolidate if appropriate.

Private task/project names, thread identifiers, account details, local paths, source code, screenshots, and private URLs are omitted.

items.title: [macOS][CLI 0.156.1] Corrupted thread_history_1.sqlite header blocks Desktop/CLI; recovery requires history rebuild

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

On **2026-10-09**, Codex Desktop and CLI stopped functioning normally. The live `~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite` could not be opened:

```text
sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database
```

The original database was roughly **722 MB**, not a missing or empty file. Its first 16 bytes did **not** contain the mandatory `SQLite format 3\0` header; they resembled a SQLite index-leaf B-tree page at file offset zero. The cause of this corruption is **unknown**; no power loss, checkpointing race, application bug, or filesystem fault has been established.

A staged Rust-based restoration using the surviving session JSONLs and rebuilt history database brought **both Desktop and CLI back up**. The original corrupted database has been retained locally.

## Environment

- macOS, Apple Silicon
- Codex CLI: **0.156.1**
- Codex Desktop: affected; exact build not captured
- On-disk Codex home: `~/.codex`
- Available disk space at diagnosis: ~683 GB

Initial app-server status had `status: "notRunning"` and `managedCodexVersion: null`; whether this was a cause or a consequence is unknown.

## Forensic evidence

```text
$ file ~/.codex.original-backup-*/thread_history_1.sqlite
.../thread_history_1.sqlite: data

$ od -An -tx1 -N16 ~/.codex.original-backup-*/thread_history_1.sqlite
 0a 00 f0 00 53 00 c5 00 0f 54 0f 29 0e fe 0e d3
```

Expected SQLite header:

```text
53 51 4c 69 74 65 20 66 6f 72 6d 61 74 20 33 00
```

The leading `0x0a` **resembles** a SQLite index B-tree leaf page marker, followed by apparently structured page bytes. This observation alone does **not** prove a page was relocated or identify the writer responsible.

The live `state_5.sqlite` remained readable and contained **8,008** thread records, and all their JSONL rollout paths existed. The history database was the immediate blocker.

## Recovery and validation

1. In an isolated Codex home, reconstructed history from **7,554** session copies.
2. Recovered `state_5.sqlite` passed `PRAGMA quick_check` and contained **7,554** threads.
3. Rebuilt `thread_history_1.sqlite` passed `PRAGMA quick_check`, was normally reopenable, and contained:
   - **11,224** `thread_turns`
   - **194,304** `thread_items`
   - **7,554** `thread_history_projection_state` entries
4. All **7,554** history projection byte offsets matched EOF line boundaries of the recovered JSONLs.
5. The live state had **454** additional threads not in the reconstructed history: **453 legacy**, **1 paginated**. Their JSONL files were preserved.
6. A Rust utility cloned the live `~/.codex` into a separate staging directory, overlaid recovered JSONLs and the repaired history DB, preserved the live state and additional threads, and validated the stage.
7. Activated the staged home while retaining a timestamped backup of the original.
8. **Result: Desktop and CLI are running again.**

Caveat: the one extra live-only paginated thread did not have a rebuilt projection during this recovery; it was preserved for later verification.

## Actual vs expected

**Actual:** an invalid derived history SQLite file prevented normal use of Codex history/Desktop/CLI, requiring extensive manual recovery.

**Expected:** Codex should detect an unreadable history database, retain the original and its journal companions for diagnostics, and provide a safe supported rebuild from the intact JSONL sessions. It should not present intact conversation data as irrecoverable.

## Request for maintainers

- Investigate how the history database's page-zero SQLite header could be replaced with page-like bytes.
- Check startup, migrations, concurrent Desktop/CLI app-server access, database replacement, WAL handling, and checkpoint paths, without assuming any is the cause.
- Add validation and safe self-recovery for `thread_history_1.sqlite` and preserve original files for forensic review.
- Ensure recovery merges or preserves threads created since the last usable projection.

## Related reports

- #44595 (macOS damaged history database after an *explicitly reported* power outage; **no such cause confirmed here**)
- #35091 (Codex state/SQLite corruption and lost conversation access)

## Privacy

No raw SQLite files, rollouts, transcript contents, authentication files, account identifiers, or personal filesystem paths are attached. The original damaged file is preserved locally should the maintainers request a privacy-preserving way to collect diagnostics.

**Reproduction trigger:** unknown; only the resulting invalid file and the successful staged restoration have been verified.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI

### What feature would you like to see?

Allow users to override individual MCP tool descriptions and names through user-level configuration.

Tool names and descriptions help Codex determine which tool to use for a given request. However, users consuming third-party MCP servers cannot tailor those descriptions or names to their workflow. This can lead Codex to repeatedly choose the wrong tool even when a more suitable MCP tool is available.

### Example

In my setup, Codex frequently chooses Playwright MCP for browser automation even when a service-specific MCP tool supports the requested operation natively. 

Now, Playwright is extremely useful when it’s the right tool for the job, but I'm having to append “do not use Playwright” to almost every initial prompt which is not sustainable haha

Playwright is also just one example here; the same issue can apply to any overlapping MCP tool capabilities.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Desktop app: `26.1007.21159` (CFBundleVersion `20052`), verified from the installed app's Info.plist; About dialog was not accessible to the agent.
The installed `unified-computer-use` plugin is also `26.1007.21159` and enabled.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.2, build 25F84, verified with `sw_vers`.

### What issue are you seeing?

On October 10, 2026, a previously working Safari daily check-in task stopped at the first Computer Use call, before returning a URL, accessibility tree, screenshot, or page state:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Safari");
```

Exact tool output:

```text
This session has been stopped because Computer Use is not allowed on the current browser URL. Stop your work and send a final message noting why the session has been ended. Note that Computer Use is not allowed on this URL even if the user navigates to it themselves.
```

The task's fixed destination was `https://glados.rocks/console/checkin`. After the failure, the user confirmed that Safari's current foreground address bar showed this URL. Because the initial tool call did not return a URL, the exact browser URL at the original failure is not independently verified.

The user also checked the application's Computer Use settings and confirmed that permission for any application was enabled. The error does not explain which URL was blocked, which rule or policy source made the decision, or whether this is an intentional restriction, a site classification false positive, or a URL-detection problem.

The same bounded Safari workflow successfully completed the check-in on October 9. The current plugin cache was installed later that day, but an update-related cause has not been established.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence, not retried after the safety stop:

1. Run the desktop app with Computer Use and its unified plugin enabled.
2. Request a Safari task that reuses the existing login state and operates only the fixed GLaDOS check-in page.
3. Call `cua.getApp("Safari")`.
4. The tool returns the URL safety-stop message above before any page observation or browser input.
5. Separately, the user confirms that Safari is currently at the fixed URL and that general application permission is enabled.

Reproducibility in a fresh session has not been established. No reload, check-in click, credential entry, CAPTCHA handling, or attempt to bypass the restriction was performed after this failure.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please identify whether this URL is intentionally restricted or whether a regression or false positive is involved. If access is intentionally denied, the error should provide an actionable explanation distinguishing URL safety restrictions from application authorization and URL-detection failures, and explain which normal settings can or cannot resolve it.

This report does not request disabling or bypassing safety checks.

### Additional information

- Read-only local configuration checks found no explicit `browser_use`, `computer_use`, or `allow_browser_and_computer_use` denial in the user's config. This does not rule out app-side or remotely delivered policy.
- The runtime distinguishes `blockedURL = -10015` from `permissionsNotGranted = -10009`.
- Failure-window system logs contain `AccessibilitySupport.UIElementError Code=2`; its relationship to the URL block is unknown.
- An attempt to open the desktop application's feedback UI through Computer Use was separately rejected with `Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.` The self-targeting restriction is already reported in #23452; it is mentioned only to explain why this report uses GitHub rather than the in-app feedback UI.
- No account details, credentials, cookies, private filesystem paths, raw logs, screenshots, or session transcripts are attached.
