items.title: [macOS] Composer dictation requires activating macOS keyboard Dictation before every recording

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT/Codex macOS desktop app **26.1007.21159**, build **20052**, bundle ID `com.openai.codex`. Built-in update check on October 9, 2026 returned `up_to_date` on the prod channel.

### What subscription do you have?

Not specified in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS **15.7.4**, MacBook Pro with built-in microphone.
`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The microphone button beside the message composer does not reliably activate usable microphone capture. This concerns **speech-to-text dictation**, not live voice chat.

The user reports that during failed attempts the macOS orange microphone-use indicator does not appear. Activating **macOS keyboard Dictation** while Codex dictation is waiting immediately enables Codex recording. macOS Dictation can then be stopped, and Codex continues recording normally for that attempt. However, the next recording needs the same manual activation again.

Switching chats also reproduces the problem, and returning to the previously working chat does not reliably recover it. There is no confirmed root cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

User-reported repeatable sequence:

1. Open a chat and click the composer's microphone button.
2. Attempt to speak. Codex does not capture usable speech, and the user does not see the macOS orange microphone-use indicator.
3. Press the keyboard key that starts **macOS system Dictation**.
4. Codex microphone capture starts working.
5. Stop macOS Dictation. Codex continues recording normally and can transcribe the recording.
6. Finish the Codex recording and start another one, including after switching chats.
7. The failure recurs; starting macOS Dictation again is required.

### What is the expected behavior?

Every press of the composer microphone button should start usable microphone capture without first activating a separate system Dictation session.

### Additional information

**Troubleshooting already performed, without a persistent fix:**

- Verified the system default microphone is the built-in MacBook Pro microphone.
- Tested both the specific built-in microphone and **System default** in the app's Voice settings.
- Switched the system input away and back.
- Fully quit and reopened the application; also restarted the Mac.
- Reset the app's microphone authorization.
- Backed up system audio preferences, restarted `coreaudiod`, and reset microphone/speech-recognition authorizations.
- Verified a fresh application process was started after that reset; the issue still occurred.
- Checked for an application update; none was offered.

Camo and NDI virtual inputs and an iPhone Continuity input are present. Their involvement has **not** been established; none was removed.

**Diagnostic observations, with limits:**

- One earlier startup request reached `device_requested` but never reached `microphone_ready` or `first_audio` before cancellation roughly 18 seconds later.
- Other requests reached `microphone_ready`, `first_audio`, and `recording_started`, including after a full relaunch. These log entries cannot be mapped conclusively to every failed user interaction.
- Read-only inspection of the installed frontend indicates that `first_audio` can be emitted for a nonempty buffer before meaningful signal is checked. Thus this stage alone does not establish audible microphone capture.
- The observed behavior suggests a capture-initialization/lifecycle interaction, but this is a hypothesis, not a confirmed diagnosis.

Please investigate why briefly activating macOS Dictation restores capture for only one Codex recording attempt.

A bounded search of existing issues did not identify this exact per-recording macOS Dictation activation workaround. No private conversations, screenshots, credentials, account identifiers, local usernames, or raw diagnostic logs are included. Prepared and submitted at the user's request.

### Update: macOS upgrade did not resolve the issue

The user upgraded macOS from **15.7.4** to **15.8.1 (24H32)** and reports that dictation still does not work normally. The installed OS version was independently verified locally after the upgrade. The app remains **26.1007.21159**, build **20052**. This confirms that the tested OS update did not resolve the reported failure; the underlying cause remains unconfirmed.

### Update: reinstall did not resolve the issue

On October 9, 2026, the user reports downloading and reinstalling the app and that the microphone problem still persists. The reinstalled app version and exact reinstall procedure have not been independently verified. No clean removal of local application data is claimed.

### Update: realtime voice also fails; Bluetooth disabled; new chats only temporarily work

The user now reports that disabling Bluetooth did not resolve the issue. Existing chats still fail; a new chat can initially accept dictation, then also stops working as the conversation continues. This is user-reported behavior, not a controlled comparison.

The installed app version was independently rechecked after reinstall: **26.1007.21159 (20052)** on **macOS 15.8.1 (24H32)**.

New local log evidence on October 9, 2026:

- **20:57:34.882 UTC:** realtime voice startup failed with `NotReadableError`, `errorMessage="Microphone is already in use"`, at `CODEX_REALTIME_VOICE_STARTUP_OPERATION_MICROPHONE_SETUP`.
- **20:57:43.707 UTC:** composer dictation reported the same `NotReadableError` and message.
- Later attempts reached `microphone_ready` / `first_audio` and some completed, while the user continues to report intermittent failures. These events alone do not establish consistent usable capture or whether the system-Dictation workaround was used.

This identifies microphone setup as the failure stage for those recorded attempts. It does **not** identify a competing process or prove a leaked recording resource. Capture lifecycle or routing remains a hypothesis involving the app, its capture component, and/or macOS; no hardware fault has been established.

### Update: user suspects onset after an app update

The user clarified that the suspected triggering update was the GPT/ChatGPT desktop app's **Check for updates**, not the subsequent macOS upgrade. This is the user's recollection; the exact onset is not independently confirmed.

Historical local startup logs establish different desktop build numbers:

- October 7, 2026 at approximately **14:31 PDT**: build **13536** was running.
- October 8, 2026 at approximately **19:24 PDT**: the retained logs first show the current build **20052** (currently verified as **26.1007.21159**).

These are observed startup times, not verified installation-completion times. A version regression is now an important hypothesis, but this timeline alone does not prove causation. Reinstalling left the app on build 20052, so it was not an old-versus-new version comparison.


### Update: disabling Audio visualizer restored voice input in the user's immediate test

On October 9, 2026, after reading related reports #42998 and #44596, the user disabled **Audio visualizer** in the desktop app settings. The user immediately reported that voice input worked again in the current conversation and also in other conversations.

This is the first user-reported recovery in this investigation after changing that setting, including the previously problematic conversation switching. The previous system Dictation activation workaround and repeated restarts/resets had not provided a persistent solution.

Evidence limits: this is a user-reported one-way disable comparison. We have not performed a controlled re-enable test or established long-term stability. Dictation and realtime voice were not separately confirmed in this final check. The running app version at this exact recovery was not independently rechecked; an older installer had been downloaded and extracted, but no successful rollback is established. The exact underlying implementation defect remains unconfirmed.

The result is consistent with the Audio visualizer / system-audio capture interaction documented in #42998 and #44596. Please consider these reports when investigating microphone startup and conversation switching. No private chat contents, recordings, or raw logs are included.

items.title: Tabs and line breaks silently dropped from `exec_command` `workdir` and apply_patch paths (`PathUri::join`)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

When a path contains a tab, LF or CR, Codex drops those characters and uses
a different path. If the workspace has a directory `config.txt<TAB>x` and
the model runs `exec_command` with `"workdir": "config.txt\tx"`, Codex
starts the command in `config.txtx`. That directory doesn't exist, so the
command never starts. The model is told:

```
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)\")" }
```

A process trace confirms the process-setup helper is started with cwd
`<workspace>/config.txtx`. apply_patch resolves its paths the same way, so a
file `x.md<TAB>x` is written as `x.mdx`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?


1. In the workspace: `mkdir "$(printf 'config.txt\tx')"`
2. Have the model call `exec_command` with
   `{"cmd": "ls", "workdir": "config.txt\tx"}` (`\t` is a real tab in the JSON).
3. The call fails with the error above.

### What is the expected behavior?

The command runs in `config.txt<TAB>x`, the directory the model named. If
such paths aren't supported, Codex should refuse them with a clear error
instead of silently using another path. For comparison, on the same call
OpenCode runs in the real directory, and Gemini CLI rejects the path with
"Path contains invalid characters (newlines or control characters)".


### Additional information

Root cause: `core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/exec_command.rs:203`
resolves `workdir` with `PathUri::join`, and so does apply_patch
(`apply-patch/src/parser.rs:90`). `PathUri::join`
(`utils/path-uri/src/lib.rs:528`) and `path_uri_from_segments`
(`utils/path-uri/src/absolute_path_normalization.rs:43`) add each name with
`PathSegmentsMut::push`/`extend`. The `url` crate parses that input and,
following the WHATWG URL spec, strips ASCII tab and newline from it.
`Url::from_file_path` does not have this problem; it encodes a tab as `%09`.

items.title: npm: 0.162.1 tagged latest but @openai/codex@0.162.1-win32-x64 / -win32-arm64 not published; Windows CLI fails to start

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
`@openai/codex@0.162.1` is tagged `latest` on npm, but its Windows platform packages were never published. Every Windows install or self-update to 0.162.1 leaves a CLI that cannot start.

### Evidence

`package.json` of 0.162.1 declares:

```json
"optionalDependencies": {
  "@openai/codex-win32-x64": "npm:@openai/codex@0.162.1-win32-x64",
  "@openai/codex-win32-arm64": "npm:@openai/codex@0.162.1-win32-arm64"
}
```

but:

```
> npm view @openai/codex@0.162.1-win32-x64 version
npm error 404 No match found for version 0.162.1-win32-x64
```

The dist-tags confirm it: `latest`, `darwin-x64` and `linux-x64` point to 0.162.1, while `win32-x64` and `win32-arm64` still point to 0.162.0 (`darwin-arm64` too).

### Repro (Windows 11 x64, Node 24.19.0, npm global install)

1. Run `codex` on 0.162.0 and accept the self-update (or run `npm install -g @openai/codex@latest`).
2. Run `codex`:

```
Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-win32-x64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
    at findCodexExecutable (.../@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:107:9)
```

The suggested reinstall reproduces the same failure, since npm skips the missing optional dependency silently.

### Workaround

```
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.162.0
```

### Ask

Publish `0.162.1-win32-x64` / `-win32-arm64` (or move `latest` back to 0.162.0), and consider gating the `latest` tag on all platform packages being published. This recurs: #17423, #11744.

items.title: Validate Windows sandbox accounts before password repair
items.body:
Validate Windows sandbox accounts before password repair

## Why

A credential mismatch can trigger setup that rotates both sandbox account passwords. Before allowing repair, validate the account that logged on successfully and ensure that neither account has been replaced or has an unowned runtime registration.

## What changed

- Validate runtime records and successful logon tokens, checking account SIDs, rejecting administrators, and requiring enabled `CodexSandboxUsers` membership.
- Before repair, verify recorded account SIDs and reject existing same-family package registrations for unrecorded accounts. Propagate package-query failures while allowing initial migration when no registrations exist.

## Testing

Add tests for malformed records and unrelated logon errors, plus an ignored disposable Windows Sandbox fixture covering successful logons, group membership, SID changes, migration, and unowned registrations.

items.title: Reject reserved Serde JSON keys in code mode
items.body:
Reject reserved Serde JSON keys in code mode

## Why

JavaScript objects containing Serde's reserved JSON keys can be reinterpreted during deserialization, allowing nested `RawValue` markers to bypass the parser's normal recursion limit.

## What changed

Reject `$serde_json::private::RawValue` and `$serde_json::private::Number` object keys before passing V8's serialized JSON to `serde_json`. Report a `reserved JSON object key` serialization error while continuing to allow marker text in strings and longer keys.

## Testing

Add runtime regression coverage for nested and escaped marker keys, recursion limits, normal JSON conversion, and session recovery without overwriting stored values. Extend the host-backed integration test to verify that stored values remain available across turns after rejection.

Please document and, where missing, support this workflow on Linux ARM64:

items.title: [macOS] SSH-started app-server competes with Desktop Remote Control, causing persistent active-writer conflicts for an idle thread

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Environment

- macOS, Apple Silicon.
- Desktop version observed in logs: `26.1007.21159`.
- Desktop-bundled app-server: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- A separate long-lived npm-installed app-server was also running under the same user and Codex home. Its exact in-memory version was not established.

## Observed behavior

A remote desktop client repeatedly failed to send a message to an existing thread with:

```text
thread-store conflict: thread <redacted> already has an active writer
```

Disconnecting the Codex SSH connection did not resolve the failure.

Read-only inspection on the host established:

1. The Desktop app-server reported the target thread as `idle`; its latest turn was `completed`, with no pending input.
2. `lsof` showed that the Desktop app-server held the thread writer-lock file.
3. The separate background app-server returned an empty `thread/loaded/list`, with no next page, and reported the same thread as `notLoaded`.
4. Six failed `thread/resume` requests were logged by that background app-server after the target turn had completed.
5. The background app-server held the Remote Control connection, while the Desktop app-server repeatedly received:

```text
HTTP 409 Conflict
{"detail":"Remote app server already online"}
```

Both processes referenced the same Remote Control registration.

## Startup evidence

The background process command was:

```text
codex -c features.code_mode_host=true app-server --listen unix://
```

The installed Desktop SSH bootstrap implementation uses `nohup` to launch this command, with the same log destination observed on the host. This strongly suggests an SSH bootstrap origin, but the original launch event was not retained.

## Recovery and verification

After confirming that the background app-server had no loaded threads, we attempted `codex app-server daemon stop`. It reported that the running server was not managed by the daemon manager.

We then sent `SIGTERM` only to the verified idle background app-server. The Desktop app-server subsequently changed from `Errored` to `Connected`.

No thread, database, lock file, or project data was deleted or manually modified during recovery. The target thread remained idle with its completed turn intact. Remote message delivery from the other desktop remains to be retested.

## Expected behavior

Desktop and SSH-started app-servers sharing a Codex home should coordinate Remote Control and thread ownership, or provide a clear, safe handoff procedure. A connected remote host should not repeatedly route thread-resume attempts to an instance that cannot acquire the thread.

The single-writer safeguard should remain intact.

## Limitations

This is an observed incident with process-level evidence, not a clean-room deterministic reproducer. An automatic update has not been established as the trigger.

Related: #37403, #44449, #28862.

No private thread IDs, project names, account or device identifiers, private paths, credentials, or raw session attachments are included.

Add retention annotations to submitted tool outputs

## What changed

Add `TurnInput::AnnotatedResponseItem` with a caller-supplied `retain` annotation. ## Testing

Add an integration test covering retention metadata during turn start, steering, idle submission, and rollout storage. Verify that ordinary outputs remain unmarked and model requests contain neither `retain` nor `client_authored`.

items.title: Windows elevated sandbox: cwd junction always fails under C:\Users\Default since runner became profile-free (#34629)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

26.1007.2314.0 (Microsoft Store), bundled CLI `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`. Also seen with bundled CLIs 0.159.x and 0.162.0-alpha.2.

### What subscription do you have?

Not plan-specific (Windows elevated sandbox internals)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

The elevated Windows sandbox command runner tries to create its cwd junction under `C:\Users\Default` and always fails:

```
[2026-10-09 21:03:40.132 codex-command-runner-0.162.0-alpha.17.2.exe] junction: failed to create C:\Users\Default\.codex\.sandbox\cwd: Access is denied. (os error 5)
```
(OS message translated from a localized system.)

My local sandbox logs (`%CODEX_HOME%\.sandbox\sandbox.*.log`) contain **394** of these lines between 2026-07-25 and 2026-10-09, all for `C:\Users\Default`, across several runner versions (0.159.0-alpha.12.1, 0.159.2, 0.162.0-alpha.17.2).

There are only **2** successful `junction: created` lines, both from **before 2026-07-21**, and both went to the sandbox account's real profile (`C:\Users\CodexSandboxOffline\.codex\.sandbox\cwd\<hash> -> <cwd>`).

The failure is non-fatal: `effective_cwd` falls back to the requested cwd. But this means the cwd-junction mechanism from #8444 ("use a junction for the cwd while read ACLs are being applied") has effectively been dead since 2026-07-21.

### Root cause (from source at `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2`, unchanged on `main`)

1. `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/bin/command_runner/win.rs` `effective_cwd()` uses a junction whenever `READ_ACL_MUTEX` exists, i.e. while the async read-ACL run is in progress.
2. `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/bin/command_runner/win/cwd_junction.rs` builds the junction root from the **`USERPROFILE` env var**:
   ```rust
   let userprofile = std::env::var("USERPROFILE").ok()?;
   let junction_root = junction_root_for_userprofile(&userprofile); // %USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\cwd
   ```
3. #34629 ("Harden Windows elevated sandbox startup", a26f219f67, 2026-07-21) changed the runner launch in `elevated/runner_client.rs` from `LOGON_WITH_PROFILE` to `dwLogonFlags = 0` ("Sandbox users have no profile state that commands should inherit"). Today only the opt-in registered-alias path uses `LOGON_WITH_PROFILE`.
4. Because no profile is loaded and `lpEnvironment` is NULL, `CreateProcessWithLogonW` builds the runner's environment from the default profile, so `USERPROFILE=C:\Users\Default`. The sandbox user (`CodexSandboxOffline`/`Online`) cannot write there, so `create_dir_all` fails with error 5 and `create_cwd_junction` returns `None`.

So the two changes are inconsistent. #34629 made the runner profile-free, but `cwd_junction.rs` still assumes `USERPROFILE` points at the sandbox account's own profile.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Windows, `windows.sandbox = "elevated"`, `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`.
2. Trigger a launch while the async read-ACL run is still active, e.g. the first command right after an app update or after adding a new read root. In my log, a read-ACL run was active at 21:03:40 and logged `read ACL run completed` at 21:04:01.
3. Run any sandboxed command, e.g. `codex sandbox --permission-profile :workspace -C <dir> -- powershell -NoProfile -Command Get-Location`.
4. `%CODEX_HOME%\.sandbox\sandbox.<date>.log` shows `junction: failed to create C:\Users\Default\.codex\.sandbox\cwd: ... (os error 5)`. A launch made after the read-ACL run completes doesn't attempt the junction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Either:
- the junction is created somewhere the sandbox user can actually write, so the #8444 protection keeps working for cwds whose ancestors are not yet readable; or
- if the junction is intentionally obsolete after #34629, the code path is removed (or logs at debug) instead of failing on every read-ACL window.

### Additional information

Impact: low, and no command failures observed. The fallback to the real cwd works whenever the cwd is already readable by `CodexSandboxUsers`. The remaining risk is the case #8444 was written for: during the first read-ACL run for a new read root, a cwd under not-yet-readable ancestors may fail to start.

Possible fixes:
- Put the junction root in a directory that setup provisions as writable for the sandbox group, derived from `CODEX_HOME` rather than `USERPROFILE` (e.g. under `%CODEX_HOME%\.sandbox\`). `req.codex_home` is already passed into the spawn request.
- Or resolve the sandbox account's profile directory explicitly (`GetUserProfileDirectoryW` / `ProfileList`) instead of trusting `USERPROFILE`.
- Or skip the junction attempt when the runner was started without a profile.

Workarounds such as creating `C:\Users\Default\.codex` or granting the sandbox users write access there should **not** be recommended. `C:\Users\Default` is the template for new user profiles.

Related: #8444 (introduced the junction), #34629 (switched the runner to profile-free logon).

codex-cli 0.162.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

windows with wls 2 distro ubuntu

### What issue are you seeing?

## Description

When using the Codex CLI, the `codex_apps` MCP server fails to initialize due to an OAuth authentication error (`HTTP 401 - token_revoked`).

Running `codex logout` followed by `codex login` does not resolve the issue. The MCP server continues to fail during initialization.

However, logging out using the `/logout` command **inside the interactive Codex agent**, then restarting Codex with `codex` and completing the prompted authentication flow, successfully resolves the problem.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Codex CLI.
2. Encounter the `codex_apps` MCP authentication error.
3. Exit Codex.
4. Run `codex logout` in the terminal.
5. Run `codex login` to authenticate again.
6. Start Codex and observe that the MCP authentication error persists.

## Actual Behavior

The `codex_apps` MCP server fails to initialize with the following error:

```text
MCP client for `codex_apps` failed to start:
MCP startup failed: handshaking with MCP server failed.

HTTP 401:
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Encountered invalidated oauth token for user, failing request",
    "type": null,
    "code": "token_revoked",
    "param": null
  },
  "status": 401
}

MCP startup incomplete (failed: codex_apps)
```

## Expected Behavior

Running `codex logout` followed by `codex login` should correctly refresh or replace the OAuth credentials used by the `codex_apps` MCP server, allowing it to initialize successfully.

## Workaround

The following procedure successfully resolved the issue:

1. Open the interactive Codex CLI using `codex`.
2. Execute `/logout` inside the Codex agent.
3. Exit the agent.
4. Run `codex` again.
5. Complete the authentication flow prompted automatically by Codex.

After following these steps, the MCP server initializes without the authentication error.

## Possible Cause

There may be an inconsistency between the authentication state cleared by the CLI-level `codex logout` command and the interactive `/logout` command.

The CLI logout/login flow may not be properly clearing or refreshing the OAuth token associated with the `codex_apps` MCP server.

This is a hypothesis based on the observed behavior and has not been independently verified.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

run codex logout and codex login on wsl terminal

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

items.body:
## Summary

In a long-running **ChatGPT Work task on Windows**, I asked the agent to bring a live website (D: drive) up to date with new features on a separate E: drive site. It reported success after approximately 35 minutes, but only after multiple follow-up challenges did it clarify that **one newly transferred feature in two files** accounted for the visible change and that multiple previously discussed website features were still unfinished. It also treated an alleged GM-layout approval requirement as a gate to other work; I dispute having authorized that gate for this deployment.

I later changed the selected model from **GPT-6.1 Sol to GPT-6 Astra**, after which I observed more meaningful follow-through. During this extended exchange I also observed approximately **3–4 context-optimization/compaction notices within about five minutes**. The exact placement of those notices relative to the model switch and the internal cause are **not independently verified**.

This report concerns **task continuation, scope/acceptance handling, potentially invented blockers, and truthful completion reporting**. It does *not* establish a backend bug, prove that the E-to-D synchronization itself was incomplete, or establish that either model or compaction caused the behavior.

## Environment / limitations

- Product: ChatGPT **Work** in the Windows desktop experience (rather than a Codex CLI reproduction).
- Subscription at time of event: ChatGPT Pro 200.
- Models visible in the transcript: **GPT-6.1 Sol**, subsequently **GPT-6 Astra** (model-change banner). Exact served-model backend routing, reasoning configuration of the earlier turns, app build, and task/thread ID have not been verified.
- Incident discussed on **October 9, 2026** (US Eastern); the visible conversation includes an overnight run and subsequent daytime follow-ups. I am not asserting precise task start or compaction timestamps.
